connect.host_key_text: The fingerprint of {host} is below. Connect only if it matches one you got from the machine's administrator or checked on the machine yourself.
connect.intro: Pick the machine where the equipe daemon runs. The next launch connects to the last one you picked.
connect.new_machine: A machine seen for the first time
connect.remember_failed: Couldn't add the key: {why} — it asks again next time
connect.remember_note: The password isn't saved. Instead this Mac's own SSH key is added to that machine once, so reconnecting after sleep or a new network doesn't ask.
connect.remembered: Added this Mac's key to {who} — no password from now on
connect.slow_reach: No answer yet. Check that the computer is on and not asleep, and on a network this Mac can reach (the same Wi-Fi, a VPN or Tailscale).
connect.slow_sign_in: Waiting to sign in. If a box is asking for a password or a confirmation, answer it.
connect.slow_open: equipe is starting on that computer. The first time can take a moment.
connect.secret_note: What you type goes to SSH and is dropped right away. Nothing is saved.
connect.ssh_first_time: New to SSH? Turn on Remote Login on the machine to connect to (Mac: System Settings → General → Sharing) and install equipe there too. Passwords aren't saved, and a machine seen for the first time connects only after you check its fingerprint.

daemon.upload_no_answer: The daemon didn't confirm it received the image

design.ask_designer: Ask the designer to make one
design.ask_designer_message: Please make a design system from the product as it is now. Put it in the design/ folder of the squad’s folder: tokens.json (W3C Design Tokens format — colour, type, spacing, radius, shadow and motion, light and dark), guidelines.md, assets/ (logos, icons, illustrations) and components/ (rendered previews of the key components). Hand it in for review when it’s ready.
design.ask_pm: Ask the PM to bring in a designer for it
design.ask_pm_message: We need a design system. The team has no designer: propose adding one, and once they join, give them a ticket to make one from the product as it is now — tokens.json (W3C Design Tokens format), guidelines.md, assets/ and components/ in the design/ folder of the squad’s folder.
design.assets_note: Transparency shows as a checkerboard. Click one to see it big and download it.
design.colors_note: Click a colour to copy its hex, a name to copy the token. Contrast is WCAG’s, against the background (a surface: against the text).
design.copy_folder: Copy the folder’s path (on the daemon’s Mac)
design.daemon_too_old: The equipe daemon this window is attached to can’t show a design system. Update equipe on the daemon’s Mac.
design.draft_banner: This is T-{id}’s draft, “{title}”. It isn’t the design system until you accept it.
design.empty_assets: assets/ — logos, icons, illustrations, and component previews
design.empty_guidelines: guidelines.md — the rules: what to use when
design.empty_text: A design system pins down your product’s colours, type, spacing, corners, shadows, motion and logos in one place. Once the designer keeps one, every member builds with the same values — and you can see and check them here.
design.empty_tokens: tokens.json — colour, type, spacing and motion values (light and dark)
design.fix_message: The design system screen couldn't read {count} things in the design tokens — for example: {examples}. Please fix tokens.json (W3C Design Tokens with $value, or plain values under named groups like color, space, radius) and hand it in again.
design.motion_note: Rest the pointer on a row to play it at its own speed and curve.
design.no_one_to_ask: There’s no one to ask yet. Add a designer to the team first.
design.nothing_yet: Nothing to show yet — once tokens can be read, they show here.
design.problems_hint: What could be read shows below.
design.sample_body: Body text looks like this. A comfortable measure and line height keep long passages easy to read. Check the figures 0123456789 and the punctuation too.
design.sample_line: Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow
design.shadow_note: Each shadow drawn as it is, on the design system’s own background.
design.spacing_note: Each bar is drawn at its real size.
design.title: Design system
design.type_note: Each style set in its own font. A font this Mac doesn’t have says what stands in for it.
diff.comments_hint: R sends the comments together as one request for changes
diff.none: No lines differ from the base branch
disk.confirm_text: Only what's listed goes. Branches stay, and build output is made again on the next build. What's removed can't be brought back.
disk.done_skipped.one: {count} item changed meanwhile and was left as it is
disk.done_skipped.other: {count} items changed meanwhile and were left as they are
disk.fix_builds_desc.one: {count} folder · made again on the next build
disk.fix_builds_desc.other: {count} folders · made again on the next build
disk.foot: equipe never removes open tickets' work, changes not committed, branches, or files outside its own folders
disk.nothing: Nothing equipe may clean right now. See below what you can clear yourself
disk.partial: Some folders took too long to count to the end: ≥ means at least that much
disk.subtitle: {host}'s disk · what takes the space, and what can go
disk.title: Disk
doc.cut: Showing the first {size} KB — open it in its app for the rest
engines.ask: {engine} {window} limit at {used}% · resets in {span} — move {names} to {to} from their next ticket?
engines.browser_desc: A browser opened on {host}. Once you finish there, it shows here.
engines.claude_not_read: Shown after a Claude member's next turn
engines.code_desc: {url} · valid for 15 minutes. Enter it only for a sign-in you started.
engines.code_title: Enter this code in the browser
engines.codex_not_read: Codex usage hasn't been read yet
engines.confirm_sign_out_desc: The {tool} CLI’s login on {host} is removed. {name} members can’t work until you sign in again.
engines.fail_device_off: Turn on “device code authorization” in ChatGPT → Settings → Security, then retry. On a workspace account, an admin turns it on.
engines.fail_expired: It wasn't finished in time. Try again.
engines.fail_lost: The connection to the daemon dropped.
engines.fail_no_answer: The daemon didn't answer. It may be older than this app.
engines.foot: Each CLI keeps its login on {host}. equipe never reads or moves it.
engines.hand_over: {engine} reached its limit · resets in {span} → handing {names}'s work to {to}
engines.hand_over_ask: {engine} reached its limit · resets in {span} — hand {names}'s work to {to} now?
engines.hand_over_why: The reset is more than an hour away. The work so far is committed and summarized, and carries on on the other engine.
engines.install_desc: Install it on {host}, then come back here.
engines.legacy_desc: The codex CLI’s login is recommended. You can remove the older one in a terminal.
engines.made: {names}: {engine} {window} limit at {used}% → {to} from the next ticket
engines.mode_auto_about: Moves members from their next ticket and tells you — one click undoes it
engines.mode_suggest_about: Asks before moving anyone when a plan runs low
engines.move_why: Members finish what they're doing and switch from their next ticket. A summary of the work goes with them, so nothing is done twice.
engines.no_answer: The daemon doesn't say where the engines stand
engines.no_answer_desc: It may be older than this app. Restart it when the squad is idle.
engines.note: No one is moved mid-turn, and no credits or extra usage are spent.
engines.person_why: Each moves between tickets — its work so far handed over, never mid-turn. It stays there until you move it again.
engines.pitch_claude: Connect Claude Code and members can edit files and commit to branches.
engines.pitch_codex: Connect Codex and the squad shares the work across two plans, so it runs into limits less.
engines.return: {engine} {window} limit is back down to {used}% → {names} return to {engine} from their next ticket
engines.return_why: The original engine has room again. Each member goes back once it finishes what it's doing.
engines.settings_foot: equipe watches what's left of your Claude and Codex plans and, as one runs low, moves its members to the other engine from their next ticket. No one is moved mid-turn, and no credits are spent.
engines.settings_setup_desc: Get the setup where Claude writes and Codex reviews proposed again
engines.setup_note: Each member switches from its next ticket. You can see this again any time in Settings › Team.
engines.setup_title: The recommended way to use Claude and Codex together
engines.setup_why: Claude writes; Codex reviews and does QA. A reviewer on a different engine than the writer catches more of what was missed, and both plans get used evenly.
engines.step_down: Both engines are near their limits → {names} on lighter settings
engines.step_down_ask: Both engines are near their limits — put {names} on lighter settings?
engines.step_down_why: Neither plan has room to spare. Instead of switching engines, members carry on with a lighter model and less thinking, and new tickets wait for the reset.
engines.switch_account_tip: Sign in again with a different ChatGPT account — it replaces this one on the daemon's machine
engines.terminal_desc: {tool} walks you through signing in in the browser. It shows here once done.
engines.usage_no_windows: {plan} plan · no 5-hour or weekly limit to show
engines.usage_soon: Remaining usage will show here soon
engines.usage_unknown: Shows after a member’s next turn
engines.who_claude: Claude plan · you sign in with your own claude
engines.who_codex: ChatGPT plan · the codex CLI’s login, connected from here
failure.app_too_old_step_menu: Update the app from the equipe menu → Check for Updates…
failure.app_too_old_step_site: Or get the latest app from equipe.im
failure.app_too_old_text: The daemon on {name} speaks protocol {daemon} and this app speaks {app}, so this app can't keep up.
failure.auth_step_copy_id: Register the key on that machine — this is the only time it asks for that machine's password
failure.auth_step_keygen: Create a key if you don't have one (skip this if `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` exists)
failure.auth_step_user: Check the user name (you can enter it as `user@host`)
failure.auth_text: The user name or password is wrong, or this Mac's SSH key isn't registered on that machine. Signing in with a key is easiest — no password every time.
failure.closed_text: Reconnecting. It picks up again on its own once the daemon is up or the network is back.
failure.daemon_off_text: Run `equipe` in a terminal to start the daemon. This window connects as soon as it's up.
failure.daemon_too_old_text: The daemon on {name} speaks protocol {daemon}; this app speaks {app}. Update equipe on that machine and it will connect.
failure.daemon_too_old_title: equipe on {name} is older than this app
failure.daemon_unavailable_step: Run `equipe` on that machine yourself and see whether the same message appears
failure.daemon_unavailable_text: equipe is on {name}, but its daemon couldn't be reached or started. The message below says why.
failure.host_key_changed_step_ask: Ask the machine's administrator why the key changed
failure.host_key_changed_step_remove: If it really did change, remove the old key and try again
failure.host_key_changed_text: The key this Mac remembers differs from the one that address presents now. The machine may have been reinstalled or the address may point to another machine — but someone could also be in the middle, so the app won't allow this connection.
failure.host_key_changed_title: The host key of {name} is different
failure.host_key_refused_step_compare: Compare it with the output of `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` on that machine
failure.host_key_refused_step_retry: Press Try Again to see the fingerprint again
failure.host_key_refused_text: This Mac hasn't seen {name} before. It connects only after you confirm the fingerprint belongs to that machine.
failure.host_key_strict_step_ssh: Connect once from a terminal with the command below to check and add the fingerprint
failure.host_key_strict_text: ~/.ssh/config sets `StrictHostKeyChecking yes`, so the key of {name} isn't added automatically.
failure.login_off_step_linux: Linux: install and start an SSH server — the command below is for Debian/Ubuntu (for other distributions, look up how to enable sshd)
failure.login_off_step_mac: Mac: System Settings → General → Sharing → turn on Remote Login (macOS 12 and earlier: System Preferences → Sharing). Check which users are allowed in, too
failure.login_off_step_port: If you changed the port, enter it again as `host:port`
failure.login_off_text: {name} isn't accepting SSH connections — most likely Remote Login (the SSH server) is off on that machine. Turning it on once, at the machine, is enough.
failure.no_bridge_text: equipe on {name} lacks `equipe attach`, which this app uses. Update equipe on that machine and it will connect.
failure.no_equipe_step_install: Install equipe with the line below (with Homebrew: `brew install equipe-labs/tap/equipe`)
failure.no_equipe_step_ssh: Sign in to that machine from a terminal
failure.no_equipe_step_wait: Once it's installed, this window reconnects on its own (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` and Homebrew folders are found automatically)
failure.no_equipe_text: Couldn't find the `equipe` command on {name}. This app is a window onto that machine's equipe daemon, so equipe must be installed there too.
failure.no_kept_path: the other machine didn't say where it kept the file
failure.no_squads_remote_step_run: Go to a project folder and run `equipe`
failure.no_squads_remote_step_ssh: In a terminal, sign in to that machine with the first line below
failure.no_squads_remote_step_wait: Once there is a squad, this window connects on its own
failure.no_squads_remote_text: The daemon on {name} has no squads. Run equipe once in a project folder on that machine to create one.
failure.no_squads_text: Run `equipe` once in a project folder to create a squad. This window will then connect on its own.
failure.other_text: The exact cause is unknown. Check the message below. Connecting to the same host from a terminal shows more detail.
failure.sign_in_cancelled_text: Signing in to {name} takes a password or a verification code. The password isn't saved; SSH keeps it only while the connection lasts.
failure.squads_unreadable: the daemon's squad list is unreadable
failure.step_retry_below: When done, press Try Again below
failure.step_retry_when_ready: Press Try Again when you're ready
failure.unreachable_step_awake: Make sure the machine is on and not asleep
failure.unreachable_step_name: Check the name or address (typos; `.local` names are only visible on the same Wi-Fi)
failure.unreachable_step_ssh: Check that `ssh` to the same host works from a terminal
failure.unreachable_step_public: {address} is an internet (public) address. The router on that computer's side has to forward the SSH port to it — easier and safer: turn on Tailscale on both computers and connect to its 100.x address
failure.unreachable_step_private: {address} only works inside a home or office network. This Mac has to be on the same network (the same Wi-Fi) — from elsewhere, turn on Tailscale on both computers and connect to its 100.x address
failure.unreachable_step_tailnet: This is a Tailscale address. Check that Tailscale is on on both computers and signed in to the same account
failure.unreachable_step_vpn: If it's on another network, you need a private network such as a VPN or Tailscale
failure.unreachable_text: Couldn't connect to {name}. The name or address may be wrong, the machine may be off (or asleep), or it may be on another network.
failure.update_remote_step: Update on that machine and restart the daemon — working members pause briefly, then carry on
header.all_projects_note: Work outside projects too · the squad's folder
header.add_project_hint_here: Type a folder's path on this Mac and press ⏎ — a folder that isn't there is made, and one that isn't a git repository is started as one
header.add_project_hint_there: Type a folder's path on the connected computer and press ⏎ (e.g. ~/code/app) — a folder that isn't there is made, and one that isn't a git repository is started as one
main.banner_reconnecting: Reconnecting — picks up on its own once it's back
main.install_text: This app is a window onto the equipe daemon. Paste the line below into a terminal to install equipe, then run `equipe`. Once the daemon is up, this window connects on its own.
main.remote_daemon_started: Just started the remote daemon — run `equipe daemon install` once on that machine to keep it always on
main.update_daemon_line: equipe on {place} is {theirs} — the app is {ours}. Update it so the new features and fixes run there too
main.update_daemon_short: equipe on {place} is {theirs} · the app is {ours}
main.update_daemon_done: Updated — the daemon restarts once its members are idle, and the app reconnects on its own
main.update_daemon_done_short: Updated · restarts once its members are idle
main.update_daemon_restarting: Restarting the daemon — the app reconnects on its own
main.update_on_quit: The update installs when you quit the app
notify.browser_body: {site} · do it yourself in the browser panel · {squad}
notify.browser_handed_body: {site} · click to do it in the app's browser panel · {squad}
notify.browser_handed_title: {member} is waiting for you in its browser
notify.browser_sign_in_title: {member} is waiting for you to sign in, in its browser
notify.failed_body: {squad} · see what went wrong in the conversation
notify.merge_conflict: It conflicts with main; nothing was merged
notify.merge_failed: The merge failed; nothing was merged
notify.send_waits: · sending waits for a person's permission
notify.sheet_body: Even with equipe behind other windows, macOS notifications tell you when a member asks permission, work is ready for review, or the conversation you last wrote in gets its answer. macOS asks once when you turn them on.
notify.sheet_private: A notification only says who needs what — never commands, passwords or file contents. Change it any time in Settings ▸ General ▸ Notifications.
notify.sheet_title: Notify you while the window is out of sight?
notify.stale_daemon: The daemon runs an older version ({version}) — restart it with `equipe daemon restart` while members are idle
notify.test_line: This is a test notification — click it
notify.update_found_body: Downloading it — you’ll be told when it’s ready
notify.waiting_body: {by}Something only a person can do is left
overview.hq_or_menu: or right-click a project in the sidebar
overview.hq_text: When you run several products, keep the roadmap, a brief of each product, decisions, runbooks and regular reports in one project. Made the HQ, it stays at the top of the sidebar, and the PM files work across the projects and on running them there.
overview.no_projects: No projects yet — add one with + in the sidebar
overview.subtitle: Each project's stuck work, reviews, work in progress and what finished this week
overview.title: Overview
pair.asked_text: Allow it only if it's your phone. It will see the squad, answer requests one at a time and talk with members.
pair.busy_text: Another window, or `equipe pair` in a terminal, has a code open. Close it there and try again.
pair.devices_unknown: Can't tell which phones are connected
pair.devices_unknown_desc: equipe on {host} is out of date. Update it and run `equipe daemon restart`.
pair.disconnected_text: Get a new code once {host} is back.
pair.expired_text: A code works for 5 minutes. Get a new one and scan it.
pair.foot: Phones talk to this machine through the {relay} relay, end-to-end encrypted.
pair.foot_connected: Phones talk to this machine through the {relay} relay, end-to-end encrypted · relay connected
pair.forget_desc: This phone won't reach the squad again. To use it, connect it anew.
pair.no_app: No app yet? Find “equipe” in the App Store on your iPhone. If the camera won't do, copy the link and paste it in the app.
pair.no_devices_desc: A phone shows here once it's connected.
pair.opening_text: equipe on {host} is opening a pairing code at the relay.
pair.paired_text: Your squad is on your phone now.
pair.private: Everything between your phone and this squad is end-to-end encrypted. The relay can't read it.
pair.refused_text: That phone wasn't connected. Get a new code to connect another one.
pair.relay_text: Phones connect through the equipe relay. Check the internet connection of the machine the daemon runs on and try again.
pair.settings_pair_desc: See the squads on {host} and answer requests in the equipe app on your iPhone. One QR scan does it.
pair.step_open: Open the equipe app on your iPhone
pair.step_scan: Point it at this code, then click Allow here
pair.step_settings: Tap Settings › Pair with a computer
pair.subtitle: See the squads on {host} and answer requests from your phone.
pair.title: Scan with the equipe app on your iPhone
pair.too_old_text: equipe on {host} is older than this app and can't pair a phone from here. Update equipe there and run `equipe daemon restart`. Until then, `equipe pair` in a terminal works.
pair.unavailable_text: The daemon on {host} couldn't start pairing phones. Run `equipe daemon restart` there and try again.
peek.ask_cancel: Cancel T-{id}? Its member stops; the branch stays.
peek.ask_changes: What should change? It goes to {who}
peek.ask_memo: Say what you did; it goes with T-{id} (optional)
peek.ask_method: How should T-{id} land this time?
peek.memo_and_go: Add a note and carry on
peek.why_accepted_only: It was accepted but not merged into main yet.
peek.why_conflict: Merging into main hit a conflict, so nothing was merged. {detail}
peek.why_kept: You chose to keep it on its branch. You can still merge it into main any time.
peek.why_way_ask: This project asks each time. This time it was accepted without merging.
peek.why_way_branch: This project is set to leave accepted work on its branch.
relaunch.label: Restart to Update · {version}
render.diagram_failed: Couldn't draw this diagram; here is its source.
render.file_not_here: This file isn't on this Mac — path copied: {path}
roadmap.empty: Nothing to draw yet. Hand the PM some work and it shows up here.
roadmap.subtitle: Each project: done → now → next → waiting; an arrow points from what must finish first
roadmap.title: Roadmap
routines.empty: Set up regular operations work — a weekly report, a dependency check — and the PM starts it at its time. What the PM does shows in the conversation and tickets as usual, and anything that needs your permission still asks you.
routines.form_hint: Times follow the clock of the Mac the daemon runs on
routines.name: Name
routines.need_what: Say what the PM should do
routines.preset_deps_prompt: Check each project for outdated dependencies and security advisories. List what should be upgraded with its risk, and propose the updates needed as tickets.
routines.preset_morning_prompt: Give me this morning's briefing: what finished yesterday, what's on today, and only what I need to decide or check.
routines.preset_weekly_prompt: Sum up the past week project by project: what finished, what's in progress, what's stuck and what I need to decide, and next week's plan. With an HQ, keep it there as a dated document under reports, and give me a short summary.
routines.subtitle: Handed to the PM when their time comes
routines.title: Routines
routines.what_placeholder: e.g. Sum up the past week project by project
sent.gone_tip: Uploaded files are cleared after a week
settings.appearance_desc: Follow the Mac, or keep it light or dark
settings.auto_update_desc: Checks every hour and downloads in the background
settings.blocked_desc: Things never allowed, whoever asks: sudo, wiping the disk, force-pushing
settings.browser_panel_desc: Beside the conversation, the page a member sees
settings.browsers_shown_desc: Off, members browse hidden; the panel always shows them
settings.check_updates_desc: Look for a new version now
settings.connection_foot: ⌘⇧K picks a machine too. The one picked reconnects next time.
settings.disk_desc: Room enough · see what takes the space and clean up
settings.follow_project: Show only the chosen project's conversation
settings.follow_project_desc: With a project chosen at the top, the PM's conversation shows only what was said about it. Off: the whole conversation, whatever the project.
settings.intro_about: This app's version, updates, and where to learn more.
settings.intro_browser: The Chrome members share: whether it shows on screen, and how sign-ins work.
settings.intro_engines: The AI your members work with. Each platform signs in with its own CLI; equipe never reads that login.
settings.intro_general: Settings for this Mac's window only: language, look, what it opens on, notifications.
settings.intro_keys: Every key the app answers to. Type a key or what it does in search to find it.
settings.intro_permissions: What members may do on their own and what they must ask you first. For the whole squad.
settings.intro_projects: The repositories the squad works on, and how accepted work lands in each.
settings.intro_squad: The squad this window follows, the machine its daemon runs on, and settings the squad keeps.
settings.intro_team: Each member's model, thinking effort and mode. They apply from its next turn; the conversation carries on.
settings.key_board: Switch between the work board and the conversation
settings.language_desc: The words of menus and screens
settings.links_desc: Where links in replies open · ⌘-click opens them in the other
settings.language_note: The language is shared by every equipe screen on this Mac, the terminal included. System follows the language macOS gives equipe — set one for equipe alone in System Settings › General › Language & Region › Applications.
settings.link_docs_desc: Design notes and the desktop app guide
settings.mac_screen: Members may use this Mac's screen
settings.mac_screen_desc: Off: whoever has it lets go at once (/desktop stop) · every squad
settings.machine_local_desc: The daemon runs on this Mac
settings.machine_ssh_desc: The daemon runs on {host}, reached over SSH
settings.mode_ask_desc: Asks you before every edit and every command
settings.mode_auto_desc: Edits, installs and tests on its own inside its worktree; asks before network, pushes or your accounts
settings.mode_foot: ⌘⇧M changes it from the composer too.
settings.mode_full_desc: Does anything your account can without asking, except what is always blocked; still asks before acting in your name
settings.no_members_desc: The team shows here once the daemon is connected
settings.no_projects_desc: Tell the PM about a repository and it shows here
settings.no_rules_desc: Answer a request with “Always” (⇧A) and that kind of thing lands here
settings.notifications_allowed: Allowed · banner style and sounds are in macOS System Settings
settings.notifications_denied: Off in macOS, so none arrive — turn on Allow Notifications in System Settings › Notifications › equipe
settings.notifications_foot: Only while the window is out of sight; in sight, the sidebar and cards say it. Connected to another Mac's daemon, notifications still come to this Mac.
settings.notifications_no_bundle: A dev build run outside the app bundle can't send notifications (the Dock number still shows)
settings.notifications_not_asked: Not allowed yet — macOS asks once when you turn them on
settings.ping_approvals_desc: When it wants to do something its mode doesn't allow
settings.ping_badge: Show a number on the Dock icon
settings.ping_badge_desc: How many things wait in Inbox, on equipe's Dock icon
settings.ping_failed_desc: When an error stops a member's turn
settings.ping_merged_desc: When accepted work lands on main. A failed merge is told under “A turn fails”
settings.ping_replies_desc: When the conversation you last wrote in gets its answer, with its first line
settings.ping_reviews_desc: When a member hands in a finished ticket
settings.ping_sound_desc: Play the system sound with each notification
settings.ping_update_desc: When a new version is downloaded — it installs when you restart
settings.ping_waiting_desc: Something only a person can do, like signing in or paying
settings.pop_out_desc: For what a picture can't do — a passkey, a permission prompt — the panel's button opens the real window
settings.projects_foot: How accepting (A) lands a branch, per project. Kept on this Mac only.
settings.restart_daemon_desc: Run this in a terminal to move to a new version; conversations carry on
settings.rules_foot: Once revoked, it asks again from the member's next turn.
settings.shared_sign_in_desc: Members' browsers use the accounts you signed in to. Acting in your name — paying, publishing — always asks first
settings.sign_in_desc: Run it in a terminal and sign in in its window; every member uses those sign-ins
settings.sign_in_foot: Sign-ins are kept on the daemon's machine and shared by every squad.
settings.squad_foot: Kept by the daemon: the same on every screen following this squad.
settings.start_desc: What the window shows when the app opens
settings.suggestions_desc: After a member answers, a greyed guess in the empty box · → takes it
settings.system_notifications_desc: If macOS has equipe's notifications off, none arrive
settings.team_foot: Model and effort apply from the next turn; the conversation carries on. “Squad's” uses the default mode under Permissions.
settings.update_downloading_desc: Keep working while it downloads. Restart once it’s ready to install it
settings.update_ready_desc: A new version is downloaded; it goes in when the app starts again
settings.zoom_desc: Makes text and everything else larger or smaller together
state.chip_kept_tip: You chose to keep this on {branch}. You can merge it into main any time.
state.chip_not_on_main_tip: Accepted, but this work is still only on {branch}, not in main.
state.not_on_main_hint: The work you accepted is only on the member's branch. Merge it to put it in main.
state.review_flash: T-{id} to review · in the Inbox, A accepts, R asks for changes
state.waiting_flash.one: T-{id} your turn — {name} asks you {count} thing
state.waiting_flash.other: T-{id} your turn — {name} asks you {count} things
term.title: Terminal · {place}
term.offered: The command to run yourself is typed into the terminal — check it and press ⏎
target.bad_chars: The host or user name has characters that aren't allowed
target.bad_port: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535
target.user_empty: The user name before @ is empty
team.back_to_board: T-{id} — goes back to the board
team.quota: Runs on your Claude/Codex plan alongside the team: usage adds up while they work at once.
team.title: Team change
tickets.comment_hint: Goes to the member on it and the PM.
tickets.confirm_body: {from} stops working on it now. The work so far stays on its branch, in its worktree, and {to} picks it up from there.
tickets.dependency_loop: That would make a loop of waiting: {path}.
tickets.depends_search: Find a ticket by words or number
tickets.drop_to_cancel: Drop here to cancel it (you'll be asked)
tickets.ev_back_to_proposal: put it back to a proposal
tickets.key_views: Views: pick one, or save this one
tickets.kind_action_hint: Does something in an app or the browser, asking before each step
tickets.kind_code_hint: Changes a project, on a branch you merge
tickets.kind_task_hint: Finds out, writes, decides — into the squad's folder
tickets.kind_under_way: T-{id} has work under way — it keeps its kind.
tickets.owner_closed: T-{id} is finished — there is no one to give it to.
tickets.owner_under_way: T-{id} is being worked on — give it to someone rather than to no one.
tickets.project_under_way: T-{id} has work under way in its project — it stays there.
tickets.quick_hint: @frontend · #web · !high · after T-12 — the rest is its title
tickets.refuse_accept_with_a: Accepting is A — it asks how the work lands
tickets.refuse_closed: Finished — send it back to work instead
tickets.refuse_handed_in_by_member: Only the member doing it hands it in for review
tickets.refuse_not_by_hand: Not by dragging — use its buttons (R sends back, A says it's done, N cancels)
tickets.refuse_starts_by_itself: Work starts when its owner picks it up — set the assignee instead
tickets.refuse_under_way: Under way — cancel it, or give it to someone else
tickets.refuse_waits_by_member: Only a member puts work down for you
tickets.shaping: Sent to the PM: it comes back as a proposal to take on.
tickets.sheet_hint: The PM and its member hear of it.
tickets.triage_banner_hint: proposals from the squad — take on or drop
tickets.triage_done: Every proposal is taken on or dropped. Esc goes back to the tickets.
tickets.triage_hint: Proposals from the squad: take one on (A) and it is ready for its owner, or drop it (N).
turn.file_copy: Not on this Mac — click to copy the path
turn.file_look: Click to look · ⌥-click to show in Finder
turn.keys: ⌘↵ sends · Tab to the next · Space picks
turn.left.one: {count} not answered stays open on the ticket
turn.left.other: {count} not answered stay open on the ticket
turn.tip_dont_know: {name} finds another way, or asks differently
turn.tip_later: {name} carries on without it — it stays open on the ticket
turn.tip_note: A word for {name} on this one
turn.tip_your_call: {name} decides, and says what it chose
turn.tip_yours: Hand it back: {name} does it — and calls you to the browser if it needs your sign-in
turn.waiting: {name} is waiting — once you send, it picks up where it left off
update.why_download: The new version couldn’t be downloaded — check your internet connection and try again
update.why_feed: The update information couldn’t be read — try again in a moment
update.why_move: An app opened from the disk image or a download folder can’t update itself — move it to Applications and open it there
update.why_other: The update hit an error (code {code}) — the log has the details
update.why_permission: No permission to write where the app is, so the update couldn’t be installed — check that it’s in Applications
update.why_signature: The downloaded update’s signature couldn’t be verified, so it wasn’t installed
